comparison.objective: Candidate commissions and locks a shock absorber through iterative physical impact testing; pr-1727 crossfades two audio channels. Meaningfully different objectives.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires hex-key engagement, setscrew unlocking/relocking, collar adjustment, counterholding, and response-based iteration. pr-1727 requires coordinated opposing travel of two linear faders. Shared bimanual fine control is only generic.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two safe stopping cycles within stroke/energy/velocity limits and retained adjustment. pr-1727 requires precise final fader positions plus continuous no-dead-air/no-double-full path constraints. Candidate omits numeric rebound, overload, drift, and tightening-torque thresholds; pr-1727 has no separate spec versions, but its body supplies detailed thresholds.
comparison.reason: The tested mechanism, manipulation sequence, feedback loop, and failure modes differ materially; missing candidate thresholds do not suggest duplication of the unrelated crossfade task.
